prompt: Build a BankVault that exercises all four Java access levels: a private balance, public deposit/withdraw/getBalance, a package-private auditReset(), and a protected isOverdrawn(). Complete the starter file, then run the tests.
explanation: Java has four access levels and each one draws a boundary: private keeps the balance field reachable only from inside BankVault, public opens deposit/withdraw/getBalance to every caller, no modifier at all (package-private) limits auditReset() to code in the same package, and protected additionally lets subclasses call isOverdrawn(). Because the field is private, the only way to change the balance is through the methods, so deposit() can enforce its rule that non-positive amounts are ignored. That is encapsulation: the class owns its data and its invariants, and the test can only observe behaviour, never poke at the field.
hints: Declare the field as `private double balance;` -- every other method in the class can still read and write it directly.
Package-private means literally no keyword: `void auditReset() { ... }`. Adding public or private would change who may call it.
isOverdrawn() just compares: the balance is overdrawn when it is less than 0.0. Remember deposit() must ignore amounts that are not greater than 0.
